title: 撕开女人‘慕强’真相！

timeline.summary: Mikey defines ‘strength’ as perceived social position and upper-position behavior rather than money, looks or credentials, using public-figure and employer/employee analogies.
He links attraction to mystery, distance, principles and controlled availability, then extends the same framework to long-term relationships and simulated breakup explanations.
He describes women as continuously testing power relations, lists consistency tests, compares bosses with subordinates, and argues that techniques are fragments of a stronger underlying state.
He equates rules, anger and willingness to lose a partner with relational strength, discusses abuse and deception through a dominance frame, then adds broad racial, regional and gender stereotypes.

He distinguishes willing generosity from reluctant spending for approval, then recounts intentionally borrowing 10,000 yuan from a partner to raise attraction while saying he now finds the method unethical and does not recommend it.

He develops a ‘rescue desire’ theory, argues that becoming compliant lowers attraction, and recommends keeping the relationship near a breakup boundary, including describing the partner as a tool and alternating availability.
He closes with an unsupported evolutionary account of attraction, claiming primitive status and reproductive cues override modern ethics and social achievement.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He defines attraction-relevant strength as the relationship's perceived hierarchy, a person's principles and their manner under pressure rather than objective wealth, looks or credentials alone.
claims.conditions: This is Mikey's interpretive framework and is already represented in formal source 9zRpsnsPGxU; it is not a validated model of all relationships.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He treats tolerating silence, refusing approval-seeking and keeping one's principles as signs of an upper-position posture.
claims.conditions: The narrow self-possession theme must be separated from his boss/subordinate analogy and from using dominance to control another person.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He argues that distance and incomplete disclosure preserve mystery and attraction, while deep disclosure and constant availability reduce it.
claims.conditions: Presented as a universal claim without comparative evidence; his examples are personal interpretation rather than independent outcome verification.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He says techniques such as push-pull are only visible fragments of a broader inner state and will fail when copied without consistent principles and behavior.
claims.conditions: Reusable only as a description of his method hierarchy; it does not validate the surrounding gender or dominance theory.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He distinguishes freely chosen generosity from spending reluctantly to buy approval or sexual access.
claims.conditions: The self-consistency distinction is narrower than his unsupported assertion that women reliably detect motive and lose attraction.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He recounts intentionally borrowing 10,000 yuan from a partner despite having money in order to increase attraction, then says he now considers the tactic unethical and does not encourage or recommend it.
claims.conditions: Manipulative financial anecdote; the negative qualification must never be omitted, and the claimed result is only his account.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He recommends sustaining long-term attraction through instability, a breakup-edge dynamic, selective availability and treating the partner as a tool.
claims.conditions: Manipulative and potentially emotionally coercive relationship framing; not suitable for action advice.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He asserts that women prefer ‘bad men’, remain attached after deception or abuse, and are driven by rescue desire.
claims.conditions: Unsupported gender generalization with victim-blaming and abuse-normalizing implications; his explicit statement that he does not encourage domestic violence does not validate the claimed mechanism.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He makes broad biological claims about women and racial claims that Black people are less civilized and therefore more criminal and more attractive.
claims.conditions: Unsupported sexist and racist essentialism; never present as fact or use to classify individuals or groups.

claims.speaker: Mikey discussing public figures
claims.statement: He infers private motives and relationship hierarchies for named public figures from selected public behavior.
claims.conditions: Third-party motive attribution is unverified and this edited upload supplies no full primary context.

examples.summary: The landlord's son, boss/employee elevator and schoolmate-on-an-e-bike stories illustrate perceived posture, but they are analogies or personal recollections, not controlled evidence.
The 2023 drinking-date and 2020 borrowing anecdotes are Mikey's own retrospective causal interpretations; no partner account or contemporaneous evidence is supplied.

speaker_attribution.speaker: Mikey
speaker_attribution.basis: Single visible host and continuous first-person narration across all sampled frames.

speaker_attribution.speaker: live commenters
speaker_attribution.basis: Several questions and short statements are read or answered by Mikey; the sparse visuals do not show a readable live-chat panel, so exact attribution remains contextual.

speaker_attribution.speaker: partners, women and public figures
speaker_attribution.basis: Only represented through Mikey's simulations, anecdotes or commentary; none provides an independent voice in this upload.

visual_findings: All 55 sampled frames were reviewed. Every frame shows the same single-host desk shot with burned-in subtitles; no chat record, document, public-figure clip or partner testimony appears in the sampled set.

The visual track supports only a talking-head classification. It does not verify public-figure claims, personal relationship outcomes, audience questions, the 10,000-yuan transfer or claims about women and racial groups.

Because sampling is at 45-second intervals, shorter overlays or gestures may have been missed. Dense continuous checks are required around high-impact anecdotes and possible audience-question transitions before exact audio-visual attribution.

permissions.reason: Edited reuse of an existing formal source plus manipulative relationship advice, unsupported group generalizations and unverified third-party claims.

limitations: Automatic transcript was read in full but not checked word-for-word against original audio; numerous homophone errors remain.
Fifty-five sparse frames do not equal continuous audio-visual verification.
The source is an edited reuse of formal source 9zRpsnsPGxU and must not add source weight or corroboration.
Claims about attraction mechanisms, public figures, abuse, deception, race and evolutionary biology are not independently verified.
